description: Static detection rules for DeepSeek exposure surface in source code, dependency manifests, container definitions and local model artifacts. Rules detect evidence of presence only; they cannot prove absence.

rules.fascsa_note: Direct calls to DeepSeek-hosted API endpoints mean prompts and data are sent to infrastructure operated by the excluded vendor. References DHS Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01 (procurement exclusion of DeepSeek products and services).
rules.name: DeepSeek hosted API endpoint
rules.remediation: Replace the endpoint with an approved model provider. If the endpoint is only in a comment or dead code, remove it and record the removal in your evidence file.

rules.fascsa_note: Configuration for the excluded vendor's API indicates an integration point, even if the key itself is not present in the repository.
rules.name: DeepSeek API credential / configuration variable
rules.remediation: Remove the variable from code, examples and deployment configuration. Rotate any real key that was ever committed, then record the change in your evidence file.

rules.fascsa_note: A DeepSeek model identifier in code or configuration indicates the product requests, loads or routes to a DeepSeek model, directly or through a gateway.
rules.name: DeepSeek model identifier string
rules.remediation: Identify the call path that uses this model id, swap it for an approved model, and re-run this scan to confirm the identifier is gone.

rules.fascsa_note: The deepseek-ai namespace on model hubs refers to first-party DeepSeek model releases (weights or configs) pulled into the product.
rules.name: DeepSeek model hub namespace (deepseek-ai/)
rules.remediation: Replace the referenced weights with an approved model release, or remove the reference if unused. Record the weight source you ship instead.

rules.fascsa_note: Importing a DeepSeek SDK (first-party or a client wrapper for the DeepSeek API) is direct evidence of a code-level integration with the excluded vendor's service.
rules.name: DeepSeek SDK import
rules.remediation: Remove the SDK usage and route the affected feature through an approved provider's SDK. Check dependency manifests too (rule DS-006).

rules.fascsa_note: A DeepSeek-named package declared as a direct dependency ships as part of the product and falls inside the third-party-products scope of Order #2026-01.
rules.name: DeepSeek package in dependency manifest (direct)
rules.remediation: Remove the package or replace it with an equivalent from an approved vendor, regenerate lockfiles, and re-run this scan.

rules.fascsa_note: A lockfile hit usually means a transitive (second-hand) dependency pulls in a DeepSeek-related package. Transitive presence still counts as part of the delivered product.
rules.name: DeepSeek reference in dependency lockfile (possibly transitive)
rules.remediation: Trace which top-level dependency pulls it in (your package manager's dependency-tree command), then upgrade, replace or explicitly exclude it and regenerate the lockfile.

rules.fascsa_note: Container definitions that pull DeepSeek images or models (for example via ollama pull deepseek-*) bake the excluded vendor's models into the deployed artifact.
rules.name: DeepSeek reference in container / deployment definition
rules.remediation: Swap the image or model pull for an approved model, rebuild the image, and re-scan the rebuilt definitions.

rules.fascsa_note: A first-party DeepSeek weight file inside the product directory is a DeepSeek implementation artifact in the most literal sense covered by Order #2026-01.
rules.name: DeepSeek model weight file (by filename)
rules.remediation: Remove the weight file from the product and from any image or bundle that embeds it. If weights were renamed, verify provenance with metadata or fingerprint tooling (see the project roadmap) rather than filenames.

rules.fascsa_note: A model config that declares a DeepSeek architecture or a deepseek source path indicates bundled DeepSeek-derived weights, even when the weight files themselves were renamed.
rules.name: DeepSeek architecture declared in model config.json
rules.remediation: Identify the weights this config belongs to, establish their provenance, and replace them with an approved model release if they are DeepSeek-derived.

vendor: DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.)
